title: Add microburst seq-workload runner and flamegraph profiling reporter
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Production traffic shows short, high-throughput microbursts and a heavy tail of sequence lengths. Existing benchmark runners in benchmark-lab focus on steady-state throughput and long-run tails; we lacked a compact runner and reporting pipeline to (1) simulate microburst arrival patterns, (2) produce deterministic profiling baselines (pprof/flamegraph), and (3) aggregate/serialize those baselines for downstream regression detection. This PR introduces a new lightweight seq-workload runner plus a profiling reporter and an upload pipeline so teams can add representative workloads and keep historical baselines.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds bench/runners/microburst_runner.py: a runner that replays token arrival patterns derived from the seq-census, supports configurable microburst shapes (sine/exponential/pulse), and has a KV-cache warmup stage to model cold vs warm starts.
- Adds bench/reporters/flamegraph_reporter.py and bench/utils/profile_convert.py: collects pprof traces, converts to folded-stack format, and writes flamegraph-friendly JSON (Flamebearer) and raw pprof artifacts.
- CI integration: bench/ci/bench_profiles.yaml runs a reduced set of microburst and steady-state workloads on PRs in the benchmark-lab repo and uploads artifacts to the internal benchmark bucket for later aggregation.
- Baseline serialization: bench/data/baselines/seq_microburst_baseline.parquet and a small shim that annotates runs with metadata (model, quantization, seq-dist, hardware).
- Docs and runbook: docs/bench/baseline-runbook.md describes how to add a new workload, interpret flamegraph output, and schedule weekly baseline collection.

Checklist (top-level):
- [x] microburst runner with config-driven workloads
- [x] deterministic tokenization and seeded RNG to make profiles reproducible
- [x] flamegraph/pprof exporter and converter to folded stacks
- [x] CI job for lightweight profile collection and artifact upload
- [x] retention tagging on artifacts and runbook docs
- [x] unit tests for core runner logic and reporter

Why this approach: The runner is intentionally small and sandboxed to keep CI cost low while producing signal-rich profiles. Using folded-stack conversion and parquet baselines allows downstream aggregation and cheap diffs for regression alerts. The KV-cache warmup stage lets us compare cold and warm steady states, which surfaced a 12-18% latency delta on internal experiments.

Risks and mitigations:
- CI artifact storage cost: mitigated by a reduced-runset on PRs and full-run scheduled weekly in a separate pipeline.
- Flaky profiles due to non-determinism: RNG seeded and tokenization checksum included in artifact metadata.
- Security: artifacts are uploaded to the internal benchmark bucket with retention tags and access controls.

Related items: ENG-4052, ENG-4127 (perf alerting work), a small follow-up will add BigQuery aggregation (ENG-4199).
commits: a1b2c3f: add microburst runner and initial configs; d4e5f6a: add pprof/flamegraph reporter and conversion utils; f7a8b9c: CI job and upload shim; 0f1e2d3: add docs and tests; fixup: make RNG seeding deterministic and reduce CI run lengths
release_notes: Adds microburst workload runner and profiling pipeline. New CI job collects lightweight profiles and uploads to internal benchmark storage. Enables flamegraph baselines for regression detection.
discussion: Diego Marquez (reviewer): Nice focused addition. Two asks: 1) can we make the microburst shapes pluggable via JSON so SRE can add real traffic shapes? 2) ensure the CI job does not run full GPU runs on every PR.

Aisha Patel (author): Reply: both addressed. Shapes are JSON-driven under bench/configs/microburst_shapes.json and the CI job only runs CPU-only, short runs; weekly profile collector runs full GPU baseline.
Lina Chen (reviewer): Tests look good but test_microburst_runner.py still used a non-deterministic sleep. Suggest using a fake clock to speed tests.
Aisha Patel (author): Reworked tests to use the testing clock fixture from tests/utils/clock_fixture.py and reduced wall time. All unit tests pass locally.

Marcus Holloway (approver): Approved after Aisha's last fix. CI artifacts are uploaded to internal-s3://benchmarks/redwood/seq_microburst/ with retention tags. I spot-checked the flamegraph output — looks sane.
